title.en: The transport layer: building a reliable connection on an unreliable network
title.zh: 传输层：在不可靠的网络上搭一条可靠的连接

description.en: Understand why reliability belongs at the two ends rather than in the routers, what loopholes sequence numbers, the three-way handshake and the release handshake each close, and how one process finds another process on a different host.
description.zh: 懂得为什么可靠性要放在两端而不是路由器里，序号、三次握手和释放握手各自堵住了什么漏洞，以及一个进程凭什么找到另一台主机上的进程。

name.en: Role and services of the transport layer
name.zh: 传输层的角色与服务 (role and services of the transport layer)
报文段与封装 (segment and encapsulation)

name.en: Simple transport primitives and the connection state diagram
name.zh: 简单的传输层原语与连接状态图 (simple transport primitives and connection state diagram)

name.en: Reliable transfer over an unreliable network: sequence numbers, acknowledgements and checksums
name.zh: 在不可靠网络上做可靠传输：序号、确认与校验和 (reliability and sequence numbers)
三次握手建立连接 (three-way handshake)
非对称释放与对称释放 (asymmetric vs symmetric release)

name.en: The two-army problem and release with timers
name.zh: 两军问题与带计时器的释放握手 (two-army problem and release with timers)

name.en: Transport-layer addressing: TSAP, NSAP and ports
name.zh: 传输层寻址：TSAP、NSAP 与端口 (addressing: TSAP, NSAP, port)
多路复用与多路分解 (multiplexing and demultiplexing)
套接字编程与 Berkeley 套接字 (socket programming)

description.en: Thinking reliability should be guaranteed by routers. Routers are stateless so that they can scale; reliability belongs at the two ends.
description.zh: 以为可靠性应该由路由器保证。路由器无状态才能扩展，可靠性放在两端。

description.en: Thinking a two-way handshake is enough. With two messages, the receiver decides the connection is established before it has heard the other side's answer, so an old duplicate request can make it open a connection all by itself.
description.zh: 以为两次握手就够了。两次握手里，接收方在听到对方的回答之前就已经认定连接建立，旧的重复请求会让它单方面开好连接。

description.en: Thinking asymmetric and symmetric release differ only in speed. Asymmetric release ends both directions as soon as a disconnect request arrives, so data still in flight is lost; symmetric release closes each direction separately.
description.zh: 以为非对称释放和对称释放只是快慢之别。非对称释放一收到断开请求就双向终止，路上的数据会丢；对称释放每个方向各关各的。

description.en: Thinking the release handshake fully solves the problem of each side knowing that the other side knows. It only lowers the risk, using retries and timeouts.
description.zh: 以为释放握手能彻底解决双方「谁先知道对方知道」的问题。它只是用重试和超时把风险压低。

description.en: Thinking a socket's LISTEN blocks. In Berkeley sockets, the call that blocks is ACCEPT.
description.zh: 以为套接字的 LISTEN 会阻塞。Berkeley 套接字里阻塞的是 ACCEPT。

description.en: Thinking accept returns the same socket that was listening. It returns a new socket.
description.zh: 以为 accept 返回的还是原来监听的那个套接字。它返回的是一个新套接字。

chapter.en: Why we need a transport layer

title.en: A packet is lost halfway through a download
title.zh: 下载到一半丢了一个包

prompt.en: You download a 1 MB file from www.unimelb.edu.au, and it is cut into several hundred packets. The network layer only does its best to deliver: packets can be lost, reordered, duplicated or corrupted. Who do you think should guarantee that you get the file without a single byte wrong?
prompt.zh: 你从 www.unimelb.edu.au 下载一个 1 MB 的文件，它会被切成几百个包。网络层只管尽力送，包可能丢、乱序、重复、损坏。你觉得应该由谁来保证你拿到的文件一个字节不差？

label.en: Every router along the way: for each packet it forwards, it checks that the next hop received it
label.zh: 沿途每个路由器：每转发一个包，都确认下一跳收到了

feedback.en: Then every router would have to keep state for every connection and do error recovery, and the network would become too complex to scale.
feedback.zh: 那样每个路由器要为每条连接记状态、做错误恢复，网络就复杂得撑不住大规模。

label.en: The transport layers at the two ends: the sender retransmits, the receiver puts things in order, and the two ends build a reliable connection themselves
label.zh: 通信两端的传输层：发送方重发，接收方整理，两端自己搭一条可靠的连接

label.en: Nobody can guarantee it; the application has to accept an occasionally corrupted file
label.zh: 没有谁能保证，应用只能接受偶尔坏文件

feedback.en: It can be guaranteed. The price is a little extra work at the two ends.
feedback.zh: 能保证。代价是在两端多做一点事。

label.en: The physical layer: make the line good enough and no packets will be lost
label.zh: 物理层，把线路做得足够好就不会丢包

feedback.en: However good the line is, congestion and faults still happen, so packet loss cannot be eliminated.
feedback.zh: 再好的线路也会有拥塞、故障，丢包无法根除。

explain.en: Only the two ends know whether the whole file has arrived, while a router handles packets from countless connections every second and should not keep books for each one. So the two ends build the reliable connection themselves and the routers stay simple. This lesson is about how the two ends build it.
explain.zh: 只有收发两端才知道「整个文件到齐没有」，而路由器每秒要处理无数条连接的包，不该替每一条记账。所以两端自己搭可靠的连接，路由器保持简单。这一课讲两端怎么搭。

title.en: The network layer and the transport layer look so alike: why two layers?
title.zh: 网络层和传输层这么像，为什么要分两层

text.en: Back to that 1 MB download. Suppose the queue of a router in the middle is full and it drops one of the packets. Who makes up for it?
text.zh: 回到那 1 MB 的下载。假设中间一个路由器的队列满了，丢掉了其中一个包。谁来补？

text.en: If the router has to make up for it, it must keep a copy of every packet until the next hop acknowledges it, and it must remember how far along each connection is. A router forwards countless connections at once, so that bookkeeping would crush it, and the network could never grow large. So the network layer is **deliberately simple and unreliable**: it does its best to deliver, and takes no responsibility if a packet doesn't arrive.
text.zh: 让路由器补，它就得把每个包留一份，等下一跳确认才能扔，还要为每条连接记着「发到哪了」。一个路由器同时转发的连接多得数不清，这笔账会把它压垮，网络也就没法做大。所以网络层**故意保持简单、不可靠**：尽力送，送不到不负责。

text.en: Letting the **two ends** make up for it is different: only your laptop and the web server each keep track of this one download, so the books are kept only by those who need them. This is why the transport layer exists: **put reliability at the two ends, and routers can be stateless and the network can scale**.
text.zh: 让**两端**补就不同了：只有你的笔记本和 Web 服务器各自记着这一条下载，账只记在需要的人手里。这就是传输层（transport layer）存在的理由：**可靠性放在两端，路由器才能无状态，网络才能扩展**。

text.en: Making it a separate layer has two more benefits. One is flexibility: how reliable to be is up to the transport protocol itself, so use TCP (connection-oriented) when you want it steady and UDP (connectionless) when you want it fast. The other is a clear division of labour: the network layer and below **provide** the transport service, and the application layer **uses** reliable transport. The application only calls a few standard service calls and does not care what network lies underneath.
text.zh: 拆成独立一层还有两个好处。一是灵活：可靠到什么程度由传输协议自己定，要稳的用 TCP（面向连接），要快的用 UDP（无连接）。二是分工清楚：网络层及以下是**提供**传输服务的一方，应用层是**使用**可靠传输的一方。应用只要调用几个标准的服务调用，不必管底下是什么网络。

text.en: The transport layer gives applications three things: **process-to-process** communication (the browser process talks to the web server process, not just host to host), **reliable transfer** (nothing lost, duplicated, reordered or corrupted), and **efficient transfer** (no needless retransmission, with flow control and congestion control).
text.zh: 传输层给应用三样东西：**进程到进程**的通信（浏览器进程对 Web 服务器进程，而不只是主机对主机）、**可靠传输**（不丢不重不乱、不出错）、**高效传输**（别白白重发，要有流量控制和拥塞控制）。

summary.en: Beyond the slides: even if every hop acknowledges, the two ends still have to check for themselves
summary.zh: 超出课件：就算每一跳都确认，两端还是得自己检查

text.en: Even if routers acknowledge hop by hop, a router could crash after receiving a packet, or corrupt the data in its memory, and the two ends would still not know. So in the end the two ends must confirm the whole thing themselves. Since the two ends have to do it anyway, doing it again in the middle is just extra overhead. This is the famous "end-to-end" idea in network design.
text.zh: 即使路由器逐跳确认，它收到后崩溃、或内存里把数据弄错，两端依然不知道。所以最后一定得由两端自己确认整件事。既然两端必须做，中间再做一遍就是多余的开销。这是网络设计里著名的「端到端」想法。

title.en: Segments: carried in packets, which are carried in frames
title.zh: 报文段：装在分组里，分组装在帧里

text.en: The messages that the transport entities at the two ends exchange are called **segments** (also called TPDUs). A segment gets a transport-layer header and is handed to the network layer as the payload of a **packet**; the packet gets a packet header and is handed to the data link layer as the payload of a **frame**. This is the layer-by-layer encapsulation from Lesson 1.
text.zh: 两端传输层（transport entity）互相交换的消息叫**报文段**（segment，也叫 TPDU）。它加上传输层头部，作为**分组**（packet）的载荷交给网络层；分组加上分组头，又作为**帧**（frame）的载荷交给数据链路层。这就是第 1 课讲的逐层封装。

title.en: Five primitives: how an application uses the transport layer
title.zh: 五个原语：应用怎样使用传输层

text.en: An application does not assemble segments itself; it calls a few **primitives** that the transport layer provides. The slides first use a **hypothetical** connection-oriented service to explain this:
text.zh: 应用不会自己去拼报文段，它调用传输层给的几个**原语**（primitive）。课件先用一套**假想**的面向连接服务说明这件事：

rows.en: none
rows.zh: 无

rows.en: Blocks, waiting for some process to connect
rows.zh: 阻塞，等某个进程来连

rows.en: Actively set up a connection
rows.zh: 主动去建立连接

rows.en: Send data
rows.zh: 发数据

rows.en: none
rows.zh: 无

rows.en: Blocks, waiting for data to arrive
rows.zh: 阻塞，等数据到

rows.en: This side wants to release the connection
rows.zh: 这一方想释放连接

text.en: A typical conversation: the server first does LISTEN and waits there; the client does CONNECT, sends CONNECTION REQ., and waits until the server replies CONNECTION ACCEPTED; after that the two sides exchange data with SEND and RECEIVE, for example the server does RECEIVE while the client does SEND; finally either side does DISCONNECT.
text.zh: 一次典型的通话：服务器先 LISTEN，停在那里等；客户端 CONNECT，发出 CONNECTION REQ.，等到服务器回 CONNECTION ACCEPTED；之后双方用 SEND 和 RECEIVE 收发数据，比如服务器 RECEIVE、客户端 SEND；最后任何一方 DISCONNECT。

title.en: This LISTEN is not the same as the one in sockets later
title.zh: 这套 LISTEN 和后面的套接字不一样

body.en: Here LISTEN blocks until someone connects. In real Berkeley sockets, LISTEN only declares "I am willing to accept connections" and gives a queue size; the call that blocks and waits is ACCEPT. We compare the two at the end of this lesson.
body.zh: 这里的 LISTEN 会阻塞，直到有人来连。真正的 Berkeley 套接字里，LISTEN 只是声明「我愿意接受连接」并给出队列大小，阻塞等待的是 ACCEPT。本课最后会对照。

title.en: The states of a connection: walking through the diagram
title.zh: 连接的状态：一幅图逐个走

text.en: A connection is in a different **state** at different moments, and it moves between states when a segment arrives or a primitive is executed. The slides' state diagram has three ways to read it: **solid lines** are the path the client takes, **dashed lines** are the path the server takes; transitions in **italics** are caused by a segment arriving, those in regular type are caused by the application executing a primitive.
text.zh: 一条连接在不同时刻处在不同**状态**（state），收到报文段或执行原语时就转移。课件的状态图有三条读法：**实线**是客户端走的路，**虚线**是服务器走的路；**斜体**的转移是因为报文段到达，**正体**的是因为应用执行了原语。

alt.en: Connection state diagram: the client (solid) goes from IDLE through ACTIVE ESTABLISHMENT PENDING to ESTABLISHED, then through ACTIVE DISCONNECT PENDING back to IDLE; the server (dashed) goes through PASSIVE ESTABLISHMENT PENDING and PASSIVE DISCONNECT PENDING
alt.zh: 连接状态图：客户端实线从 IDLE 经 ACTIVE ESTABLISHMENT PENDING 到 ESTABLISHED，再经 ACTIVE DISCONNECT PENDING 回 IDLE；服务器虚线经 PASSIVE ESTABLISHMENT PENDING 与 PASSIVE DISCONNECT PENDING

caption.en: The two paths meet at ESTABLISHED: once the connection is set up, both sides stand in the same state.
caption.zh: 两条路径在 ESTABLISHED 汇合：连接建立后，双方站在同一个状态上。

text.en: Walk through it. **Client** (right side): IDLE; the application executes CONNECT, a request is sent, and the client enters ACTIVE ESTABLISHMENT PENDING, meaning "I have started connecting and am waiting for an answer"; when CONNECTION ACCEPTED arrives, it goes to ESTABLISHED. **Server** (left side): it stays IDLE, sitting in LISTEN; as soon as CONNECTION REQ. arrives it enters PASSIVE ESTABLISHMENT PENDING, "someone has knocked and I haven't agreed yet".
text.zh: 沿着走一遍。**客户端**（右边）：IDLE，应用执行 CONNECT，发出请求，进入 ACTIVE ESTABLISHMENT PENDING，意思是「我主动去连了，在等答复」；收到 CONNECTION ACCEPTED，到 ESTABLISHED。**服务器**（左边）：一直 IDLE，停在 LISTEN 里等；CONNECTION REQ. 一到，进入 PASSIVE ESTABLISHMENT PENDING，「有人敲门了，我还没答应」。

text.en: In the diagram this step of the server is labelled "execute CONNECT", which is easy to find confusing: isn't the server in LISTEN? LISTEN's job is to wait, and once a request arrives it unblocks; the server's process then executes CONNECT, which here means "accept", CONNECTION ACCEPTED is sent back to the client, and the server enters ESTABLISHED. In sockets later, this step gets its own name, ACCEPT.
text.zh: 图里服务器这一步标着「执行 CONNECT」，容易看糊涂：服务器不是在 LISTEN 吗？LISTEN 的任务是等，请求到达后它就解除阻塞；服务器的进程随后执行 CONNECT，在这里是「接受」的意思，CONNECTION ACCEPTED 由此发回客户端，服务器进入 ESTABLISHED。后面套接字里，这一步有了自己的名字 ACCEPT。

text.en: Disconnecting is symmetric too, along two paths: the side that does DISCONNECT first (the active side) enters ACTIVE DISCONNECT PENDING, the other side enters PASSIVE DISCONNECT PENDING when it receives the request, and each returns to IDLE. **The key point: the states on the two sides are synchronised step by step through segments.**
text.zh: 断开也是对称的两条路：先 DISCONNECT 的一方（主动方）进入 ACTIVE DISCONNECT PENDING，对方收到请求后进入 PASSIVE DISCONNECT PENDING，各自回到 IDLE。**要点：两边的状态是靠报文段一步步同步的。**

title.en: CONNECTION ACCEPTED is lost on the way
title.zh: CONNECTION ACCEPTED 在路上丢了

prompt.en: Following the slides' state diagram: the server receives CONNECTION REQ., its process accepts, and it sends CONNECTION ACCEPTED, but this segment is lost on the way. What state is each side in now?
prompt.zh: 按课件的状态图：服务器收到 CONNECTION REQ.，进程接受了，于是发出 CONNECTION ACCEPTED，但这个报文段在路上丢了。这时两端各处在什么状态？

label.en: The client is still in ACTIVE ESTABLISHMENT PENDING, and the server is already ESTABLISHED
label.zh: 客户端还在 ACTIVE ESTABLISHMENT PENDING，服务器已经 ESTABLISHED

label.en: Both are ESTABLISHED, because the server has already agreed
label.zh: 两端都在 ESTABLISHED，因为服务器已经答应了

feedback.en: The client needs CONNECTION ACCEPTED to arrive before it can move to ESTABLISHED. The segment was lost, so it has not received it, and its state does not change by itself.
feedback.zh: 客户端要靠 CONNECTION ACCEPTED 到达才能转移到 ESTABLISHED。报文段丢了，它就没有收到，状态不会自己变。

label.en: Both return to IDLE, because the connection was not set up
label.zh: 两端都回到 IDLE，因为连接没建成

feedback.en: Once the server has accepted, it has left IDLE, and nobody tells it to undo that. It does not go back by itself.
feedback.zh: 服务器接受之后已经离开 IDLE，没有谁通知它撤销。它不会自己回去。

label.en: The client is ESTABLISHED, and the server is PASSIVE ESTABLISHMENT PENDING
label.zh: 客户端 ESTABLISHED，服务器 PASSIVE ESTABLISHMENT PENDING

feedback.en: This is the wrong way round. The server moves forward after it accepts, while the client moves forward only when CONNECTION ACCEPTED arrives.
feedback.zh: 这是反过来了。服务器接受后才向前走，客户端要等到 CONNECTION ACCEPTED 才向前走。

explain.en: The states of the two sides are synchronised by segments, so when one segment is lost the two sides no longer match: the server thinks it is connected, and the client is still waiting. This is the loophole we fix next, using timers, acknowledgements and sequence numbers, plus the three-way handshake. The slides' state diagram is simplified and does not draw the timers.
explain.zh: 两端的状态靠报文段同步，一个报文段丢了，两边就对不上：服务器以为通了，客户端还在等。这是下面要补的漏洞，补法是计时器、确认和序号，再加三次握手。课件的状态图较简化，没有画计时器。

hints.en: The client's transition is triggered by a segment arriving; if none arrives, it does not move.
hints.zh: 客户端的转移是「收到报文段」触发的，没收到就不动。

chapter.en: How a reliable connection is built

title.en: The reliability toolbox
title.zh: 可靠的工具箱

text.en: The network layer can deliver packets end to end, but packets may be lost, reordered, duplicated or corrupted, and many applications cannot work under those conditions. The transport layer first sets up a **connection** so the two ends exchange state, then adds a few tools, each handling one kind of fault:
text.zh: 网络层能把包端到端送到，但包可能丢失、乱序、重复、损坏，很多应用在这种条件下没法工作。传输层先建立**连接**，让两端交换状态，再配上几样工具，各管一种毛病：

rows.en: Loss
rows.zh: 丢失

rows.en: Acknowledgements (ACK) plus retransmission: if no ACK arrives, send it again
rows.zh: 确认（ACK）加重传：没收到确认就再发一遍

rows.en: Duplication
rows.zh: 重复

rows.en: Sequence numbers: recognise the second copy of the same segment and drop it
rows.zh: 序号：认出同一个报文段的第二份，丢掉

rows.en: Reordering
rows.zh: 乱序

rows.en: Sequence numbers: put segments back in order by number before handing them to the application
rows.zh: 序号：按编号重新排好再交给应用

rows.en: Corruption
rows.zh: 损坏

rows.en: Checksum: if an error is detected, treat the segment as not received
rows.zh: 校验和（checksum）：发现错了就当没收到

text.en: For sequence numbers to be useful, two rules must hold. **First, do not reuse the same sequence number within the maximum segment lifetime.** This lifetime is an upper bound that the network guarantees: a segment that has drifted in the network for this long without arriving is certainly discarded. A common value is 120 seconds (2 minutes). **Second, the sequence number space must be large enough that it does not wrap around even when sending at full speed** (wrap: use up a full cycle and come back to 0).
text.zh: 序号要有用，得守两条规矩。**第一，在最大报文段寿命（maximum segment lifetime）内不重用同一个序号。**这个寿命是网络保证的上限：一个报文段在网络里漂过这么久还没到，就一定被丢掉。常用的取值是 120 秒（2 分钟）。**第二，序号空间要大到，即使满速发送也不会回绕**（wrap，用完一圈又回到 0）。

text.en: Why? Imagine an old segment is still drifting in the network while the sequence numbers have gone round a full cycle and been taken by new data. The old segment now arrives late, the receiver sees a "valid" sequence number and cannot tell new from old, so it accepts the old data as new, and the file is corrupted. Put the two rules together: **the time for the sequence numbers to go round once must be longer than the time a segment can live.**
text.zh: 为什么？设想旧报文段还在网络里漂着，序号却已经转了一圈，被新数据用上了。旧报文段这时姗姗来迟，接收方看到一个「合法」的序号，分不清是新是旧，就会把旧数据当新数据收下，文件就坏了。两条规矩合起来，就是：**序号转一圈的时间，要比报文段能活的时间长。**

title.en: How long until the sequence numbers go round once (beyond the slides)
title.zh: 序号多久转完一圈（超出课件）

intro.en: This is a worked example beyond the slides, to get a feel for "how large the sequence number space must be". Suppose sequence numbers are 32 bits, every byte is numbered, and we send at full speed at 1 Gbit/s. How long until the sequence numbers are used up once?
intro.zh: 这是一个超出课件的算例，用来感受「序号空间要多大」。设序号是 32 位，给每个字节编号，以 1 Gbit/s 满速发送。问：多久把序号用完一圈？

why.en: The count of numbers 32 bits can encode; each byte uses one.
why.zh: 32 位能编的号码数，每个字节占一个号。

why.en: Convert bits to bytes, because sequence numbers count bytes.
why.zh: 把比特换成字节，因为序号是按字节编的。

why.en: Total number of sequence numbers divided by the number used per second.
why.zh: 总序号数除以每秒用掉的序号数。

outro.en: It takes about 34 seconds to go round once. A segment can live in the network for up to 120 seconds, much longer than that, so an old segment can easily collide with the same sequence number. The fix is to enlarge the sequence number space, or limit the speed, or shorten the segment lifetime.
outro.zh: 约 34 秒转完一圈。而报文段最多能在网络里活 120 秒，比这长得多，所以旧报文段完全可能撞上同一个序号。序号空间要加大，或者限制速度，或者缩短报文段寿命。

title.en: Are sequence numbers safe at this speed?
title.zh: 这个速度下序号安全吗

prompt.en: A connection uses 32-bit byte sequence numbers, and the maximum segment lifetime is the usual 120 seconds. The link is 1 Gbit/s and the sender sends at full speed. Is this safe? What should change?
prompt.zh: 一条连接用 32 位字节序号，最大报文段寿命取常用的 120 秒。链路 1 Gbit/s，发送方满速发送。这样安全吗？该怎么改？

label.en: Not safe: the numbers go round in 34 seconds while an old segment can live 120 seconds, so enlarge the sequence number space, or limit the speed, or shorten the lifetime
label.zh: 不安全：34 秒转完一圈，旧段还能活 120 秒，所以要加大序号空间，或限速，或缩短寿命

label.en: Safe: 32 bits give 4.3 billion numbers, which is already a big enough total
label.zh: 安全：32 位有 43 亿个号码，总数已经够大

feedback.en: The total number of values is not the point; what matters is the time to go round once compared with how long a segment can live. However large the total, a fast enough sender will go round it.
feedback.zh: 号码总数不是关键，要比的是转完一圈的时间和报文段能活多久。总数再大，发得够快也会转完。

label.en: Safe: when sending at full speed, old segments get flushed out faster
label.zh: 安全：满速发送时旧报文段会被更快地冲走

feedback.en: Sending faster only makes the sequence numbers go round faster; an old segment does not disappear earlier because of it, and it can still live out its full lifetime.
feedback.zh: 发得快只会让序号转得更快，旧报文段不会因此提前消失，它仍能活满它的寿命。

label.en: Not safe: cutting each segment smaller would solve it
label.zh: 不安全：把每个报文段切得更小，就能解决

feedback.en: Sequence numbers count bytes, so making segments smaller does not change how many byte numbers are used per second, and the time to go round stays the same.
feedback.zh: 序号是按字节编的，把段切小不改变每秒用掉多少个字节号，转圈时间不变。

explain.en: 34 seconds is less than 120 seconds: the same sequence number gets reused while the old segment is still alive. To be safe, the time to go round once must exceed 120 seconds. You can limit the speed to below about $2^{32}/120\approx3.6\times10^7$ bytes/s (about 286 Mbit/s), or enlarge the sequence number space.
explain.zh: 34 秒小于 120 秒：同一个序号会在旧段还没死的时候被重新用上。要想安全，转一圈的时间必须超过 120 秒。可以限速到约 $2^{32}/120\approx3.6\times10^7$ 字节/秒（约 286 Mbit/s）以下，或者把序号空间加大。

hints.en: First work out how long one full cycle takes, then compare it with 120 seconds.
hints.zh: 先算转一圈要多久，再和 120 秒比。

title.en: The three-way handshake: why two is not enough
title.zh: 三次握手：为什么两次不够

text.en: Setting up a connection has two goals: **one, and only one,** connection gets established, even if the segments used for setup are lost or retransmitted; and each side picks a **fresh** initial sequence number, so that the sequence number rules above have a clean starting point. The slides do it in three steps:
text.zh: 建立连接有两个目标：**一个、而且只有一个**连接被建起来，哪怕建连用的报文段丢了或被重传；双方各选一个**新鲜**的初始序号，让上面的序号规矩有个干净的起点。课件用三步做到：

svg.zh: <svg viewBox='0 0 620 270' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='14'><defs><marker id='a' markerWidth='8' markerHeight='8' refX='7' refY='4' orient='auto'><path d='M0,0 L8,4 L0,8 z' fill='#333'/></marker></defs><rect width='620' height='270' fill='#fafafa'/><rect x='100' y='20' width='20' height='240' fill='#fff' stroke='#333'/><rect x='500' y='20' width='20' height='240' fill='#fff' stroke='#333'/><text x='110' y='14' text-anchor='middle'>Host 1</text><text x='510' y='14' text-anchor='middle'>Host 2</text><g stroke='#333' stroke-width='2' marker-end='url(#a)'><line x1='120' y1='60' x2='498' y2='100'/><line x1='500' y1='130' x2='122' y2='170'/><line x1='120' y1='200' x2='498' y2='240'/></g><g text-anchor='middle'><text x='310' y='70'>① CR（seq = x）</text><text x='310' y='140'>② ACK（seq = y，ack = x）</text><text x='310' y='210'>③ DATA（seq = x，ack = y）</text></g></svg>

alt.en: Three-way handshake: CR(seq=x), ACK(seq=y, ack=x), DATA(seq=x, ack=y)

text.en: **If there were only two steps**: Host 1 sends CR, and Host 2 replies ACK and the connection counts as made. But an old CR from long ago may be drifting in the network and only now reaches Host 2. Host 2 cannot tell it is old, so it replies ACK, opens the connection and waits for data. Host 1 never wanted to connect, and Host 2 holds resources for nothing. Worse, if an old DATA then shows up, Host 2 already believes the connection is open and accepts it as real data. The root of the problem: **Host 2 has made its decision before it has heard Host 1's answer.**
text.zh: **如果只有两次**：Host 1 发 CR，Host 2 回 ACK 就算连上。可网络里可能漂着一个很久以前的旧 CR，现在才到 Host 2。Host 2 无法判断它是旧的，就回 ACK、开好连接、等着数据。Host 1 根本没想连，Host 2 白白占着资源。更糟的是，随后若再冒出一个旧的 DATA，Host 2 已经认为连接是开着的，就会把它当真数据收下。症结在于：**Host 2 在听到 Host 1 的回答之前，就已经做了决定。**

text.en: The third message plugs this hole: Host 2's ACK carries the new sequence number $y$ it has just chosen, and Host 1 must send $y$ back to it in the third message (ack = y). An old packet cannot know a freshly chosen $y$, so it cannot fake it. **Each side uses a fresh sequence number to prove that "this is a request from right now, not an old one".**
text.zh: 第三条消息就是来堵这个洞：Host 2 的 ACK 里带着它刚选的新序号 $y$，Host 1 必须在第三条里把 $y$ 回给它（ack = y）。旧包不可能知道一个刚选出来的 $y$，骗不了。**双方各用一个新鲜的序号证明了「这是此刻的请求，不是旧的」。**

title.en: How this differs from real TCP
title.zh: 和真实 TCP 的差别

body.en: In the slides' figure the third message is a DATA segment. In real TCP the third message is usually a plain ACK, and data can be sent afterwards. We will see this in the next lesson (UDP and TCP).
body.zh: 课件图里第三条是带数据的 DATA。真实 TCP 的第三条通常是纯 ACK，数据可以随后再发。下一课（UDP 与 TCP）会看到。

title.en: Two error scenarios: step by step, who rejects whom
title.zh: 两个出错场景，逐步看谁拒绝了谁

text.en: Scenario a: an old duplicate CR
text.zh: 场景 a：旧的重复 CR

alt.en: Scenario a: an old duplicate CR reaches Host 2, Host 2 replies ACK, and Host 1 replies REJECT
alt.zh: 场景 a：旧的重复 CR 到达 Host 2，Host 2 回 ACK，Host 1 回 REJECT

caption.en: Orange is the old segment arriving late.
caption.zh: 橙色是迟到的旧报文段。

items.en: An old CR (seq = x) arrives late at Host 2. Host 2 cannot tell, treats it as a new request, and replies ACK (seq = y, ack = x).
items.zh: 一个旧的 CR（seq = x）延迟到达 Host 2。Host 2 无从分辨，当作新请求，回 ACK（seq = y，ack = x）。

items.en: Host 1 receives this ACK. It never sent a new request with sequence number x, so it recognises this as fake and replies REJECT (ack = y). **It is Host 1 that rejects.**
items.zh: Host 1 收到这个 ACK。它并没有发出一个新的、序号为 x 的请求，所以认出这是假的，回 REJECT（ack = y）。**拒绝的是 Host 1。**

items.en: Host 2 receives the REJECT and gives up on this connection. No connection is established.
items.zh: Host 2 收到 REJECT，放弃这次连接。没有连接建起来。

text.en: Scenario b: both an old CR and an old DATA arrive
text.zh: 场景 b：旧 CR 和旧 DATA 都到了

alt.en: Scenario b: an old CR and an old DATA both reach Host 2; the ACK draws a REJECT, and the old DATA is rejected because its ack = z does not match y
alt.zh: 场景 b：旧 CR 与旧 DATA 都到达 Host 2；ACK 引来 REJECT，旧 DATA 的 ack = z 与 y 不符被拒绝

caption.en: Orange is the old segment arriving late.
caption.zh: 橙色是迟到的旧报文段。

items.en: The first two steps are the same as in scenario a: the old CR reaches Host 2, Host 2 replies ACK, and Host 1 replies REJECT.
items.zh: 前两步和场景 a 一样：旧 CR 到 Host 2，Host 2 回 ACK，Host 1 回 REJECT。

items.en: But after the old CR, an old DATA (seq = x, ack = z) also reaches Host 2.
items.zh: 可是旧 CR 之后，一个旧的 DATA（seq = x，ack = z）也跟着到了 Host 2。

items.en: Host 2 is now waiting for a message with ack = y, but this one has z, and $z\ne y$. **It is Host 2 that rejects.**
items.zh: Host 2 现在等的是 ack = y 的消息，这条里却是 z，$z\ne y$。**拒绝的是 Host 2。**

text.en: The ack = z in figure b is a value left over from the old connection, and it does not match the newly chosen y. In both scenarios, who rejects follows the same principle: **a fresh sequence number that does not match means an old packet.**
text.zh: 图 b 里的 ack = z，是旧连接留下的值，它对不上这次新选的 y。两个场景里，谁拒绝都是同一个道理：**新鲜的序号对不上，就是旧包。**

title.en: What happens with only a two-way handshake
title.zh: 只握两次手会发生什么

prompt.en: Suppose a connection is set up in only two steps: Host 1 sends CR, Host 2 replies ACK, and Host 2 considers the connection established as soon as it sends the ACK. A very old CR from long ago only now reaches Host 2. What happens?
prompt.zh: 假设建立连接只用两步：Host 1 发 CR，Host 2 回 ACK，Host 2 一发出 ACK 就认为连接已建立。一个很久以前的旧 CR 现在才到 Host 2。会发生什么？

label.en: Host 2 decides the connection is on without waiting for Host 1's answer, wastes resources, and an old DATA that follows might be accepted as real data
label.zh: Host 2 没等 Host 1 的答复就认定连接成立，白占资源，之后的旧 DATA 还可能被当真数据收下

label.en: No problem: Host 1 will reject after it receives the ACK, so the connection is not established
label.zh: 没有问题，Host 1 收到 ACK 后会拒绝，连接就不成立了

feedback.en: Host 1 can indeed reject, but in a two-way handshake Host 2 has already considered the connection established when it sent the ACK, and it will not wait for an answer. The rejection comes too late, and an old DATA that arrives afterwards would still be accepted.
feedback.zh: Host 1 确实可以拒绝，但两次握手里 Host 2 在发 ACK 的同时已经认定连接成立，它不会再等答复。拒绝来得太晚，旧 DATA 随后到达时仍会被收下。

label.en: Host 2's sequence number and Host 1's sequence number are the same, so the connection cannot be set up
label.zh: Host 2 的序号和 Host 1 的序号重复，所以连接无法建立

feedback.en: The two sides' sequence numbers are independent, and a repeat would not stop setup. The problem is that setup is too easy.
feedback.zh: 两边的序号各自独立，重复不会阻止建立。问题是建立得太容易了。

label.en: Routers will drop the old CR, so it never arrives
label.zh: 路由器会丢弃旧 CR，所以不会到达

feedback.en: An old segment can drift in the network for a long time, and routers do not know it is "old".
feedback.zh: 旧报文段可能在网络里漂很久，路由器并不认识它「旧」。

explain.en: In a two-way handshake, Host 2 has to decide before it can hear Host 1's answer. The third message hands the decision back: the connection counts as established only after a message echoing y arrives, and an old packet cannot do that.
explain.zh: 两次握手里，Host 2 要先做决定，才听得到 Host 1 的回答。第三条消息把决定权交回给它：必须收到回写 y 的消息，才算连接建立，旧包做不到这一点。

hints.en: Think about whether Host 2 decides the connection is established before or after it hears Host 1's answer.
hints.zh: 想想 Host 2 是在听到 Host 1 的回答之前，还是之后，认定连接成立的。

chapter.en: Releasing a connection: where it gets hard

title.en: Asymmetric release: one cut, and data is lost
title.zh: 非对称释放：一刀切，数据会丢

text.en: Once the connection is up and the data has been sent, it has to be torn down. The most direct way is **asymmetric release**: either side executes DISCONNECT and sends a DR (Disconnect Request), and as soon as the other side receives it, the connection ends in **both directions** at the same time.
text.zh: 连接建好、数据传完，要拆。最直接的拆法是**非对称释放**（asymmetric release）：任何一方执行 DISCONNECT，发出一个 DR（Disconnect Request），对方一收到，连接就在**两个方向**上同时终止。

text.en: The trouble is in "at the same time". Look at this sequence: after the connection is up, Host 1 sends two DATA segments in a row; just after Host 2 accepts the first DATA, it happens to send a DR. The two segments cross on the way:
text.zh: 问题出在「同时」。看这个时序：Host 1 建好连接后一连发出两个 DATA；Host 2 收下第一个 DATA 之后，正好发出了 DR。两个报文段在路上交错：

alt.en: Asymmetric release: Host 1 sends CR, receives ACK, sends DATA 1 and DATA 2; Host 2 sends DR after receiving DATA 1, and DATA 2 is discarded when it arrives
alt.zh: 非对称释放：Host 1 发 CR、收 ACK、发 DATA 1 和 DATA 2；Host 2 在收到 DATA 1 后发出 DR，DATA 2 到达时被丢弃

caption.en: The second DATA was sent normally, yet it is thrown away just because the other side said "disconnect" first.
caption.zh: 第二个 DATA 是正常发出的，却因为对方先说了「断开」而白白丢掉。

text.en: By the time the second DATA reaches Host 2, the connection is already over as far as Host 2 is concerned, and "no data is delivered after a disconnect request", so this data is lost. Host 1 did nothing wrong; it simply did not know the other side had just pressed disconnect.
text.zh: 第二个 DATA 到达 Host 2 时，对 Host 2 来说连接已经结束，「断开请求之后不再交付数据」，这段数据就丢了。Host 1 并没有做错什么，它根本不知道对方刚刚按下了断开。

title.en: Symmetric release: each direction closed on its own
title.zh: 对称释放：各关各的方向

text.en: **Symmetric release** treats the connection as two directions and **closes each direction separately**. One side doing DISCONNECT means "**I have no more data to send**", but it can still receive. The connection is released only after both sides have done DISCONNECT.
text.zh: **对称释放**（symmetric release）把连接看成两个方向，**每个方向单独关**。一方 DISCONNECT 的意思是「**我没有数据要发了**」，但它还能收。只有两边都 DISCONNECT 过，连接才算释放。

svg.en: <svg viewBox='0 0 520 280' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='14'><defs><marker id='rs' markerWidth='8' markerHeight='8' refX='7' refY='4' orient='auto'><path d='M0,0 L8,4 L0,8 z' fill='#333'/></marker></defs><rect width='520' height='280' fill='#fafafa'/><rect x='92' y='24' width='16' height='248' fill='#fff' stroke='#333'/><rect x='412' y='24' width='16' height='248' fill='#fff' stroke='#333'/><text x='100' y='16' text-anchor='middle'>Host 1</text><text x='420' y='16' text-anchor='middle'>Host 2</text><g stroke='#333' stroke-width='2' marker-end='url(#rs)'><line x1='108' y1='46' x2='410' y2='62'/><line x1='412' y1='80' x2='110' y2='140' stroke='#1a73e8'/><line x1='108' y1='100' x2='410' y2='132'/><line x1='108' y1='196' x2='410' y2='214' stroke='#1a73e8'/></g><g text-anchor='middle'><text x='260' y='46'>DATA 1</text><text x='170' y='120' fill='#1a73e8'>DR (Host 2: I'm done)</text><text x='250' y='116'>DATA 2</text><text x='260' y='192' fill='#1a73e8'>DR (Host 1: I'm done too)</text></g><text x='418' y='150' text-anchor='end' fill='#2e7d32'>✓ delivered</text><text x='260' y='252' text-anchor='middle'>The connection is released only after both sides have sent DR</text></svg>
svg.zh: <svg viewBox='0 0 520 280' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='14'><defs><marker id='rs' markerWidth='8' markerHeight='8' refX='7' refY='4' orient='auto'><path d='M0,0 L8,4 L0,8 z' fill='#333'/></marker></defs><rect width='520' height='280' fill='#fafafa'/><rect x='92' y='24' width='16' height='248' fill='#fff' stroke='#333'/><rect x='412' y='24' width='16' height='248' fill='#fff' stroke='#333'/><text x='100' y='16' text-anchor='middle'>Host 1</text><text x='420' y='16' text-anchor='middle'>Host 2</text><g stroke='#333' stroke-width='2' marker-end='url(#rs)'><line x1='108' y1='46' x2='410' y2='62'/><line x1='412' y1='80' x2='110' y2='140' stroke='#1a73e8'/><line x1='108' y1='100' x2='410' y2='132'/><line x1='108' y1='196' x2='410' y2='214' stroke='#1a73e8'/></g><g text-anchor='middle'><text x='260' y='46'>DATA 1</text><text x='170' y='120' fill='#1a73e8'>DR（Host 2：我说完了）</text><text x='250' y='116'>DATA 2</text><text x='260' y='192' fill='#1a73e8'>DR（Host 1：我也说完了）</text></g><text x='418' y='150' text-anchor='end' fill='#2e7d32'>✓ 交付</text><text x='260' y='252' text-anchor='middle'>两边都发过 DR，连接才释放</text></svg>

alt.en: Symmetric release: Host 2 sends DR first, but the DATA 2 that Host 1 is still sending is delivered as usual; after Host 1 finishes it also sends DR, and the connection is released
alt.zh: 对称释放：Host 2 先发 DR，但 Host 1 仍在发的 DATA 2 照常被交付；Host 1 说完后也发 DR，连接释放

caption.en: The same DR and DATA cross, but this time DATA 2 is accepted.
caption.zh: 同样是 DR 和 DATA 交错，这次 DATA 2 被收下了。

text.en: Host 2's DR closes only the direction "Host 2 sends out"; the direction "Host 1 sends in" is still open, so the crossing DATA 2 is delivered as usual. When Host 1 has finished, it also sends a DR, both directions are closed, and the connection is over.
text.zh: Host 2 的 DR 只关了「Host 2 发出去」的那个方向，「Host 1 发过来」的方向还开着，所以交错的 DATA 2 照常交付。Host 1 说完之后，也发一个 DR，两个方向都关了，连接才算结束。

text.en: **When is symmetric release enough?** When each side has a fixed amount of data and knows when it has finished sending, such as sending a file of known size: when it is done, it says "I'm done". **The cost** is extra negotiation: each direction needs its own close, a few more messages than a single cut; and each side must know "when I am finished", which makes the scheme awkward if a side does not know that itself. The deeper difficulty comes on the next page: how to get both sides to agree that "both are closed".
text.zh: **什么时候对称释放就够用？**当每一方手里的数据量是固定的，并且自己知道已经发完了，比如发一个大小已知的文件：发完了就说「我说完了」。**代价**是多了协商：两个方向各要一次关闭，比一刀切多几条消息；而且每一方都得知道「我什么时候发完」，如果自己都不知道，这套办法就不好用。更深的难处在下一页：怎样让双方对「都关了」达成一致。

title.en: The data is still on the way when DR is sent
title.zh: DR 发出时，数据还在路上

prompt.en: When Host 2 sends a disconnect request (DR), a DATA segment from Host 1 is still on its way. What happens to this DATA under asymmetric release and under symmetric release?
prompt.zh: Host 2 发出断开请求（DR）的时候，Host 1 发来的一个 DATA 还在路上。非对称释放和对称释放下，这个 DATA 各会怎样？

label.en: Lost under asymmetric, because the connection has ended in both directions; accepted under symmetric, because the DR closed only Host 2's sending direction
label.zh: 非对称下丢失，因为连接已双向终止；对称下被收下，因为 DR 只关了 Host 2 的发送方向

label.en: Lost under both, because Host 2's DR went out first and nothing is received after that
label.zh: 两种下都丢失，因为 Host 2 的 DR 先发出，之后什么都不再收

feedback.en: That is true only for asymmetric release. In symmetric release the DR only means the sender has no more data to send, and it can still receive.
feedback.zh: 这只对非对称释放成立。对称释放里 DR 只表示发送方没有数据要发了，它仍然可以接收。

label.en: Accepted under both, because the DATA was sent before the DR
label.zh: 两种下都被收下，因为 DATA 是在 DR 之前发出的

feedback.en: In asymmetric release, the connection ends in both directions as soon as the DR arrives, and data arriving after that is not delivered, whenever it was sent.
feedback.zh: 非对称释放里，连接一收到 DR 就双向终止，之后到达的数据不再交付，不看它是什么时候发的。

label.en: Accepted under asymmetric, lost under symmetric, because symmetric negotiates and is therefore stricter
label.zh: 非对称下被收下，对称下丢失，因为对称要协商所以更严格

feedback.en: It is the other way round. The extra negotiation is exactly what keeps data in flight from being lost.
feedback.zh: 反了。协商多一步，正是为了让还在路上的数据不被丢掉。

explain.en: The difference lies in what DR means: in asymmetric release it means "the connection is over", while in symmetric release it only means "I have no more data to send from my side". So only symmetric release lets data on the way arrive safely.
explain.zh: 差别在 DR 的含义：非对称里它是「连接结束」，对称里只是「我这边没有数据要发了」。所以只有对称释放能让路上的数据安全到达。

hints.en: How many directions does DR close in each of the two kinds of release?
hints.zh: DR 在这两种释放里各关掉了几个方向？

chapter.en: Releasing a connection: where it gets hard

title.en: The two-army problem: why no protocol can fully solve it
title.zh: 两军问题：为什么没有协议能彻底解决

text.en: Symmetric release needs both sides to agree that "it can be closed now". That is much harder than it looks. The slides borrow a classic story: Blue Army 1 and Blue Army 2 are on two different hills, with the White Army in the valley. The Blue armies win only if they attack **at the same time**; attacking alone means defeat. They communicate by messengers, but the messengers must cross the White Army and may be captured.
text.zh: 对称释放要求双方就「可以关了」达成一致。这件事比看上去难得多。课件借用一个经典故事：蓝军 1 号和 2 号分别在两座山上，白军在山谷里。蓝军只有**同时**进攻才能赢，单独进攻会输。它们靠信使通信，但信使要穿过白军，可能被抓。

items.en: Blue Army 1 sends a messenger: "attack tomorrow morning".
items.zh: 蓝军 1 号派人说「明早进攻」。

items.en: Army 2 receives it, but Army 1 does not know it did. Army 2 must send back an acknowledgement.
items.zh: 2 号收到了，但 1 号不知道它收到了。2 号得回一个确认。

items.en: That acknowledgement may be lost, and if Army 1 doesn't receive it, it dares not attack. So Army 1 must acknowledge once more: "I received your acknowledgement".
items.zh: 这个确认可能丢，1 号没收到就不敢进攻。所以 1 号还要再确认一次「我收到你的确认了」。

items.en: This new acknowledgement may be lost too... every extra acknowledgement needs another acknowledgement of itself, and it never ends.
items.zh: 这个新的确认也可能丢……每多一次确认，就要对这个确认再确认一次，永远没完。

text.en: The conclusion: **there is no protocol that can fully remove this uncertainty**. Applied to release: the last message can always be lost, and the side that sent it can never know whether the other side received it.
text.zh: 结论：**不存在一种协议能彻底消除这种不确定性**。放在释放上：最后一条消息总有可能丢，发出它的一方永远无法知道对方是不是收到了。

title.en: What is done in practice: a handshake with retries and timeouts
title.zh: 实际做法：握手加重试和超时

text.en: Since it cannot be removed, the risk is **brought down** to an acceptable level: use a three-way-handshake style of release, plus **a finite number of retries** and **timeouts**. The three parts each do one job: the handshake gets both sides to confirm "I am closing"; retries deal with lost messages; timeouts guarantee nobody waits forever.
text.zh: 既然消除不了，就把风险**压低**到可以接受：用三次握手式的释放，再配上**有限次重试**（finite retry）和**超时**（timeout）。三样各管一件事：握手让双方都确认「我要关了」；重试应付消息丢失；超时保证谁也不会永远傻等。

alt.en: A normal release handshake: Host 1 sends DR and starts a timer, Host 2 replies DR and starts a timer, Host 1 sends ACK and releases, and Host 2 releases when it receives it
alt.zh: 正常的释放握手：Host 1 发 DR 并启动计时器，Host 2 回 DR 并启动计时器，Host 1 发 ACK 并释放，Host 2 收到后释放

caption.en: Each DR must be acknowledged by the other side with an ACK.
caption.zh: 两个 DR 都要被对方用 ACK 确认。

text.en: Now the three failure cases, and what each end concludes:
text.zh: 再看三种出错的情形，每一端各得出什么结论：

rows.en: The last ACK is lost
rows.zh: 最后一个 ACK 丢了

rows.en: Host 1 releases right after sending the ACK; the ACK doesn't arrive, and Host 2's timer expires
rows.zh: Host 1 发完 ACK 就释放了；ACK 没到，Host 2 的计时器到期

rows.en: Host 2 releases by itself after the timeout. Both ends are closed, with no half-open connection
rows.zh: Host 2 超时后自己释放。两端都关了，没有半开的连接

rows.en: A DR is lost
rows.zh: DR 丢了

rows.en: For example the DR that Host 2 sent back is lost, and Host 1's timer expires
rows.zh: 比如 Host 2 回的 DR 丢了，Host 1 的计时器到期

rows.en: Host 1 resends its DR, Host 2 replies with a DR again, and the rest goes normally
rows.zh: Host 1 重发 DR，Host 2 再回 DR，之后正常走完

rows.en: The DR is lost N times in a row
rows.zh: DR 连续丢 N 次

rows.en: Host 1 has resent N times with no response
rows.zh: Host 1 重发了 N 次都没有回应

rows.en: Host 1 releases after N timeouts; Host 2's timer also expires and it releases
rows.zh: Host 1 在 N 次超时后释放；Host 2 的计时器也到期而释放

title.en: The risk is still there, just smaller
title.zh: 风险还在，只是小了

body.en: When the last ACK is lost, Host 2 has in fact not confirmed whether Host 1 received its DR; it just infers that "the other side has gone". That is still a guess, but thanks to timeouts and a finite number of retries both sides end up released and no connection is left hanging forever. In the extreme case (the DR lost N times in a row), Host 1 is giving up, not confirming.
body.zh: 最后一个 ACK 丢的时候，Host 2 其实没有确认 Host 1 是不是收到了它的 DR，只是推断「对方已经走了」。这仍然是猜测，不过靠超时和有限重试，两边最终都会释放，不会留下一条永远挂着的连接。在极端情况下（DR 连丢 N 次），Host 1 是在放弃，而不是在确认。

title.en: The last ACK is lost
title.zh: 最后一个 ACK 丢了

prompt.en: In the release handshake, Host 1 releases the connection immediately after sending the last ACK, but this ACK is lost on the way. What does Host 2 do?
prompt.zh: 释放握手里，Host 1 发出最后一个 ACK 后立刻释放了连接，可这个 ACK 在路上丢了。Host 2 会怎样？

label.en: Host 2's timer expires, and Host 2 releases the connection by itself
label.zh: Host 2 的计时器到期，Host 2 自己释放连接

label.en: Host 2 waits forever, because it never received the ACK
label.zh: Host 2 永远等下去，因为没收到 ACK

feedback.en: With a timer it will not wait forever. Timeouts exist precisely to prevent this kind of idle waiting.
feedback.zh: 有计时器就不会永远等。超时正是用来防这种傻等。

label.en: Host 1 finds the ACK was lost and sets up the connection again
label.zh: Host 1 发现 ACK 丢了，重新建立连接

feedback.en: Host 1 has already released and does not know the ACK was lost, so it will not set up the connection again.
feedback.zh: Host 1 已经释放，并不知道 ACK 丢了，也不会重新建连。

label.en: Host 2 immediately asks Host 1 to retransmit the ACK
label.zh: Host 2 立刻向 Host 1 请求重传 ACK

feedback.en: Host 1 no longer has this connection, so nobody can retransmit. Host 2 gives up by timeout.
feedback.zh: Host 1 已经没有这条连接，没人能重传。Host 2 靠超时放弃。

explain.en: The two-army problem shows that the last message can always be lost. The practical fix is to give each end a timer: when Host 2 times out, it releases. The risk is not eliminated, but no connection is left hanging forever.
explain.zh: 两军问题说明最后一条消息总有丢的可能。实际办法是给每一端装计时器：Host 2 超时就释放。风险没有消除，但没有连接会被永远挂着。

chapter.en: Finding the other side, and using it

title.en: Addressing: the IP address finds the host, the port finds the process
title.zh: 寻址：IP 找到主机，端口找到进程

text.en: The transport layer must say which **process** on the far end it is connecting to. The network layer uses the **network service access point** (NSAP) to identify a host's network interface, which on the Internet is the **IP address**. The transport layer uses the **transport service access point** (TSAP) to identify a process within a host, which on the Internet is called a **port**, for example port 80.
text.zh: 传输层要指明连的是远端的**哪个进程**。网络层用**网络服务访问点**（NSAP, network service access point）标识一台主机的网络接口，在互联网上就是 **IP 地址**。传输层用**传输服务访问点**（TSAP, transport service access point）标识主机里的某个进程，在互联网上叫**端口**（port），比如端口 80。

alt.en: The process on Host 1 with TSAP 1208 connects to Server 1 (TSAP 1522) on Host 2; Host 2 also has Server 2 with TSAP 1836; each host has one NSAP
alt.zh: Host 1 的进程用 TSAP 1208 连到 Host 2 的 Server 1（TSAP 1522）；Host 2 上另有 Server 2 用 TSAP 1836；两台主机各一个 NSAP

caption.en: Each host has only one NSAP, but can have many TSAPs.
caption.zh: 各主机只有一个 NSAP，却可以有很多个 TSAP。

text.en: In the figure, 1208 is the client's **own** port, usually assigned temporarily by the system. The server's port is agreed in advance: a web server listens on 80, and a client that wants a web page connects to 80; this is called a **well-known port** (the next lesson covers how ports are allocated). So to connect to a process on a remote machine, what you need to know is: **the other side's IP address plus the port number of the other side's process**.
text.zh: 图里 1208 是客户端**自己**的端口，一般由系统临时分配。服务器的端口则是约定好的：网页服务器监听 80，客户端想连网页就连 80，这叫**知名端口**（下一课细讲端口怎么分）。所以要连上远端的一个进程，需要知道的是：**对方的 IP 地址加对方进程的端口号**。

title.en: Connecting to a process on another host
title.zh: 要连上另一台主机上的进程

prompt.en: The browser on your laptop wants to connect to the web server process running on www.unimelb.edu.au. Which two pieces of information do you need to know to connect to it? Why is knowing only one of them not enough?
prompt.zh: 你的笔记本上的浏览器要连 www.unimelb.edu.au 上运行的 Web 服务器进程。要连上它，需要知道哪两样信息？为什么只知道其中一样不够？

key_points.en: You need the other host's IP address (the network-layer address, NSAP)
key_points.zh: 需要对方主机的 IP 地址（网络层地址，NSAP）

key_points.en: You need the port number the server process is bound to (the transport-layer address, TSAP, such as 80)
key_points.zh: 需要服务器进程绑定的端口号（传输层地址，TSAP，如 80）

key_points.en: The IP address only gets the packet to that host; a host runs many processes, so the port is needed to hand it to the right process
key_points.zh: IP 地址只能把包送到那台主机，一台主机上有许多进程，要靠端口才能交给正确的进程

model_answer.en: You need the destination host's IP address and the port number that the destination process is bound to. The IP address gets the packet to that host (network layer), but the host runs many processes at the same time, and the port number says which one to hand it to (transport layer); for example a web server is normally on port 80. With only the IP and no port, the packet arrives but does not know whom to go to; with only the port and no IP, the packet cannot find the host at all.
model_answer.zh: 需要目的主机的 IP 地址和目的进程所绑定的端口号。IP 地址负责把包送到那台主机（网络层），但主机里同时运行着很多进程，端口号才能指明交给哪一个进程（传输层），比如 Web 服务器通常在 80 端口。只有 IP 没有端口，包到了也不知道交给谁；只有端口没有 IP，包根本找不到主机。

explain.en: The IP address plus the port number. The IP finds the host and the port finds the process inside the host; you need both.
explain.zh: IP 地址加端口号。IP 管找到主机，端口管找到主机里的进程，两样缺一不可。

title.en: Multiplexing: one IP address, many conversations
title.zh: 多路复用：一个 IP 地址，许多场对话

text.en: A host usually has just one IP address (NSAP), yet it has a browser, mail and a downloader running at the same time. With multiple TSAPs, many conversations can go on at once over the same NSAP.
text.zh: 一台主机通常只有一个 IP 地址（NSAP），却同时开着浏览器、邮件、下载软件。靠多个 TSAP，同一个 NSAP 上就可以同时进行多场对话。

items.en: **Multiplexing**: hand the segments of different applications to the **same** NSAP, to be sent out through the network layer.
items.zh: **多路复用**（multiplexing）：把不同应用的报文段交给**同一个** NSAP，经网络层发出去。

items.en: **Demultiplexing**: after receiving a segment from the NSAP, look at the port number inside it and hand it to the **right** application.
items.zh: **多路分解**（demultiplexing）：从 NSAP 收到报文段后，看里面的端口号，交给**正确的**应用。

text.en: A small example. On your laptop the browser and a mail client are both open. A segment sent by the browser has source port 50123 and destination port 80 in its header; one sent by the mail client has source port 50124 and destination port 25 (the SMTP port for sending mail). Both kinds of segment are handed to the laptop's only IP address and go out through the same network layer. This is **multiplexing**.
text.zh: 一个小例子。你的笔记本上浏览器和邮件客户端同时开着。浏览器发出的报文段，头里写源端口 50123、目的端口 80；邮件客户端发出的，写源端口 50124、目的端口 25（发信的 SMTP 端口）。两种报文段都交给笔记本唯一的 IP 地址，从同一个网络层出去，这是**多路复用**。

text.en: When the replies reach the laptop, the destination IP is the same for all of them. The transport layer then reads the destination port: 50123 goes to the browser and 50124 goes to the mail client. This is **demultiplexing**. The IP address only gets the packet to this laptop; the port handles the last step, which process it goes to.
text.zh: 回信到了笔记本，目的 IP 都是它。传输层再读目的端口：50123 交给浏览器，50124 交给邮件客户端，这是**多路分解**。IP 地址只管把包送到这台笔记本，端口管最后一步，交到哪个进程手里。

text.en: It is like a dormitory building with a single street number, where each room has a room number: the courier (IP packet) delivers by street number to the ground floor, and the doorkeeper (the transport layer) hands it to the person by room number.
text.zh: 就像一栋宿舍楼只有一个门牌，每个房间有房号：快递（IP 包）按门牌送到楼下，门卫（传输层）按房号分给人。

title.en: A segment with destination port 50124 arrives
title.zh: 一个目的端口为 50124 的报文段到了

prompt.en: On your laptop, the browser uses port 50123 and the mail client uses port 50124. A segment with destination port 50124 reaches the laptop through the network layer. What should the transport layer do?
prompt.zh: 你的笔记本上，浏览器用端口 50123，邮件客户端用端口 50124。一个目的端口为 50124 的报文段经网络层到了笔记本。传输层该怎么办？

label.en: Read destination port 50124 and hand it to the mail client (demultiplexing)
label.zh: 读目的端口 50124，把它交给邮件客户端（多路分解）

label.en: Hand it to the browser, because the browser was opened first
label.zh: 交给浏览器，因为浏览器先开的

feedback.en: The transport layer doesn't look at who opened first; it dispatches by destination port. Port 50124 belongs to the mail client.
feedback.zh: 传输层不看谁先开，它按目的端口分发。端口 50124 属于邮件客户端。

label.en: Look at the destination IP address to decide who gets it
label.zh: 看目的 IP 地址决定交给谁

feedback.en: The IP address is the same for both applications and only gets the packet to this laptop. Deciding which process gets it takes the port.
feedback.zh: IP 地址两个应用相同，只能把包送到这台笔记本。分给哪个进程要靠端口。

label.en: Hand it to all processes at once and let them pick for themselves
label.zh: 同时交给所有进程，让它们自己挑

feedback.en: Then every process would have to handle data that isn't its own. The transport layer's job is to sort it out for them.
feedback.zh: 那样每个进程都要处理不属于自己的数据。传输层的任务就是替它们分好。

explain.en: IP only gets you to the host; the port gets you to the process. The transport layer reads the destination port and hands the segment to the application bound to that port; this is demultiplexing.
explain.zh: IP 只负责到主机，端口负责到进程。传输层读目的端口，把报文段交给绑定了这个端口的应用，这就是多路分解。

chapter.en: Using the transport layer in a program

title.en: Sockets: how an application actually uses the transport layer
title.zh: 套接字：应用怎样真正用上传输层

text.en: A **socket** is an endpoint of the transport layer, through which an application sends and receives data. The most common one in Internet applications is the Berkeley socket. Its primitives are a few more than the hypothetical ones we just saw:
text.zh: **套接字**（socket）是传输层的端点，应用通过它收发数据。互联网应用里最常见的是 Berkeley 套接字。它的原语比刚才假想的多几个：

rows.en: Create a new communication endpoint
rows.zh: 创建一个新的通信端点

rows.en: Associate a local address and port with the socket
rows.zh: 把本地地址和端口关联到套接字

rows.en: Declare willingness to accept connections, and give the size of the waiting queue
rows.zh: 声明愿意接受连接，并给出等候队列的大小

rows.en: Passively accept an incoming connection (blocks and waits)
rows.zh: 被动地接受一个进来的连接（阻塞等待）

rows.en: Actively set up a connection
rows.zh: 主动去建立连接

rows.en: Send and receive data on the connection
rows.zh: 在连接上发送、接收数据

rows.en: Release the connection
rows.zh: 释放连接

text.en: The call order: the **server** goes socket, bind, listen, accept, receive, send, close; the **client** goes socket, connect, send, receive, close. The client's connect triggers the three-way handshake, and the server's accept accepts it.
text.zh: 调用顺序：**服务器**是 socket、bind、listen、accept、receive、send、close；**客户端**是 socket、connect、send、receive、close。客户端的 connect 触发三次握手，服务器的 accept 接受它。

title.en: The division of labour between LISTEN and ACCEPT
title.zh: LISTEN 与 ACCEPT 的分工

body.en: Unlike the hypothetical LISTEN earlier, in Berkeley sockets LISTEN does not block; it only declares "I am willing to accept connections" and sets the queue size, and it is ACCEPT that blocks waiting for a new connection. The hypothetical LISTEN plus the "accepting" CONNECT is split here into LISTEN plus ACCEPT.
body.zh: 和前面假想的 LISTEN 不同，Berkeley 套接字里 LISTEN 并不阻塞，只是声明「我愿意接受连接」并设队列大小；阻塞等待新连接的是 ACCEPT。前面假想的 LISTEN 加上「接受」的 CONNECT，在这里拆成了 LISTEN 加 ACCEPT。

title.en: Reading the server code
title.zh: 读一遍服务器代码

caption.en: Server: the file-server example from the slides; the slides skip over the part that reads the file with an ellipsis. fatal is an error-reporting function defined in the textbook.
caption.zh: 服务器：课件的文件服务器例子，中间读文件的部分课件用省略号带过。fatal 是教材里自定义的报错函数。

items.en: `channel` holds the server's own address: `htons` converts the 16-bit port and `htonl` the 32-bit IP into the byte order the network specifies; `INADDR_ANY` means the address of any network card on this machine is acceptable.
items.zh: `channel` 里放的是服务器自己的地址：`htons` 把 16 位端口、`htonl` 把 32 位 IP 转成网络规定的字节顺序；`INADDR_ANY` 表示本机任何一块网卡的地址都可以接。

items.en: `socket(PF_INET, ...)`: PF_INET and the AF_INET above have the same value for IPv4, and the slides use both spellings. `SOCK_STREAM` is a reliable byte stream (TCP); the other kind, `SOCK_DGRAM`, is a datagram socket (UDP, next lesson).
items.zh: `socket(PF_INET, ...)`：PF_INET 和上面的 AF_INET 在 IPv4 下取值相同，课件两个写法都出现过。`SOCK_STREAM` 是可靠字节流（TCP）；另一种 `SOCK_DGRAM` 是数据报套接字（UDP，下一课）。

items.en: `SO_REUSEADDR`: after the server is shut down it can be restarted right away, without waiting for the remnants of old connections to clear before binding the same port again.
items.zh: `SO_REUSEADDR`：服务器关掉后马上重启，不必等旧连接的残余消失才能再绑同一个端口。

items.en: `QUEUE_SIZE`: while the server is busy with one connection, how many new connection requests can wait in line at most.
items.zh: `QUEUE_SIZE`：服务器忙着处理一个连接时，最多能让多少个新连接请求排队等待。

text.en: The most important point: `accept` returns a **new** socket `sa`, used only to talk to this client; the listening `s` is untouched and goes back to the start of the loop to accept the next connection.
text.zh: 最关键的一点：`accept` 返回的是一个**新**套接字 `sa`，专门用来跟这个客户端说话；监听用的 `s` 原封不动，回到循环开头继续 accept 下一个连接。

caption.en: Client: there is no bind; its own port is assigned temporarily by the system at connect.
caption.zh: 客户端：没有 bind，自己的端口由系统在 connect 时临时分配。

title.en: After accept, is the listening socket still there?
title.zh: accept 之后，监听套接字还在吗

prompt.en: In the server code, `accept(s, 0, 0)` returned the socket `sa`, and the server reads the request and writes data back on `sa`. During this time, what state is the listening socket `s` in?
prompt.zh: 服务器代码里，`accept(s, 0, 0)` 返回了套接字 `sa`，并在 `sa` 上读请求、写回数据。这期间监听套接字 `s` 是什么状态？

label.en: `s` is unchanged and remains the listening endpoint, waiting for the next accept to take the next connection
label.zh: `s` 保持不变，继续作为监听端点，等着下一次 accept 取下一个连接

label.en: `s` is `sa`; accept just gave it a different name
label.zh: `s` 就是 `sa`，accept 只是给它换了个名字

feedback.en: accept returns a new socket, which is a different endpoint from s.
feedback.zh: accept 返回的是一个新的套接字，和 s 是两个不同的端点。

label.en: `s` is closed, and the next client must bind again before it can connect
label.zh: `s` 被关闭，下一个客户端必须重新 bind 才能连

feedback.en: What is closed is `sa`, not `s`. `s` stays open all along.
feedback.zh: close 的是 `sa`，不是 `s`。`s` 一直开着。

label.en: `s` becomes the client's socket, controlled by the client
label.zh: `s` 变成客户端的套接字，由客户端控制

feedback.en: `s` is always the server's listening endpoint and has nothing to do with the client.
feedback.zh: `s` 一直是服务器的监听端点，与客户端无关。

explain.en: One listening socket can give rise to many connection sockets, one after another (or at the same time). s is in charge of "receiving guests" and sa of "serving this one guest", which is why the server can keep accepting new connections.
explain.zh: 一个监听套接字，可以先后（或同时）生出许多连接套接字。s 负责「接客」，sa 负责「服务这一位客人」，所以服务器能连续不断地接受新连接。
